Before reviewing or editing the code base, read `README.md`
to understand goals and project status.

## Rule: one headline comment per source file

Each source file must start with a comment that indicates briefly what
the file is for. This most often fits in one line, sometimes two.

Here is an example for a file named `cli/Source_delete_cmd.ml`:

```ocaml
(**
   Command-line interpretation for the [skl source delete] subcommand
*)
```

Here's another example for a file named
`base-libs/util/Text_source.ml` that provides a main type `t`:

```ocaml
(*
   A piece of text together with a name identifying where it came from
*)
```

## Comment contents

Comments are not decorative. Reading comments is expensive. Use them
to provide essential information that is not obvious otherwise, such
as but not limited to:

- why does this code exist?
- what depends on it?
- scope: intended use, known limitations, limits on how far we're
  willing to extend it
- anything that doesn't work at it should
- design choices if unusual and relevant to the reader
- first-time definitions
- simple proofs or references to proofs
- prerequisites

Make the comments readable to a human who will see the text in two
dimensions. Use single-purpose sentences. Use paragraphs to separate
topics. Use bullet points to enumerate items of a common kind.

In module interfaces, don't leak details from the module's implementation.

When it feels like you're writing excuses for complex behavior that should
be simpler, flag it as "TODO:" in its own paragraph. Then pause,
think, and propose a better interface or a refactor or better, do the
work right away.

Here's an example of a low-quality comment written by a coding agent in
September 2026:

```ocaml
val markdown_to_html : string -> string
(** Renders [markdown] to an HTML fragment (via [Omd.to_html]), meant to be
    embedded inside a larger page -- specifically, a static HTML export page
    (see Graph_export_html_cmd, this function's only real caller): a
    ["claim-ID"]/["anchor-ID"] link's [href] is rewritten to actually resolve
    there (["claim-ID.html"]; ["#anchor-ID"], an in-page fragment, since an
    anchor has no page of its own -- see [Graph.put_claim] for why every such
    reference is guaranteed a matching anchor_link rendered on that same
    page). Never emits raw HTML from [markdown]'s own content: any
    [Html]/[Html_block] node -- which [check_body]/[check_summary] normally
    reject outright, but [to_html] doesn't itself re-validate against them, so
    this doesn't only rely on that -- is rendered as its own literal,
    HTML-escaped source text instead of being passed through as markup. This
    is what keeps [to_html] safe to use on [markdown] from any source, not
    just one already known to have passed [check_body]/[check_summary] (e.g.
    an existing claim written before raw HTML was disallowed here). *)
```

Here's the same comment, rewritten to be easier to read and to modify later:

```ocaml
val markdown_to_html : string -> string
(**
    Parse and render a Markdown snippet to HTML to be embedded in the
    body of an HTML page representing a claim in the knowledge base.

    Internal hyperlink addresses of the form [claim-ID] or [anchor-ID]
    are rewritten to be valid URLs.

    Security: HTML elements found in the Markdown input are rejected,
    raising [Failure].
*)
```

Note what we did here:
- The first sentence is a synopsis that describes the action performed
  on the input and the consequences.
- The synopsis uses the imperative tense as if we were telling the
  machine what to do when calling the function.
- Each subtopic is isolated in its own paragraph.
- Sentences don't have optional clauses. If a clause can be removed,
  we removed it or we made a new sentence out of it. We keep each
  sentence focused on a single idea with a clear purpose. No rambling.
- This is not the place to explain the benefits of sanitizing external
  input or how we implemented it. We only state the guarantees we
  offer. The importance and the reason for doing this are given by the
  "Security:" prefix.

Here's another example of a bad comment:

```ocaml
type text_detail =
  | Title
  | Summary
  | Body
  | Full
      (** How much of a claim's own text to show: [Title] (just the title --
          e.g. for a search results overview, where the point is to tell
          claims apart, not read them), [Summary] (also the one-paragraph
          summary), [Body] (the full Markdown body instead -- not in addition
          to -- the summary, falling back to the summary if the claim has no
          body), or [Full] (both the summary and the body, if any).

          For a list of claims, showing one of [Summary]/[Body] is generally
          preferable to [Full]: it's cheaper to read and process a claim's
          summary alone, or its body alone, than both at once -- [Full] is
          meant for a single claim looked up on its own (see Claim_get_cmd,
          the only caller that defaults to it), not for scanning a list. *)
```

It is an enumeration. The documentation should reflect that structure:
use one comment describing each case in addition to one comment at the
type level:

```ocaml
(** How much of a claim's text to show.

    Showing the same info at different compression levels is part of
    our efforts to optimize text volume and LLM token spend. *)
type text_detail =
  | Title
  | Summary (** show title and summary *)
  | Body (** show title and body, using the summary as the body if no
             body is defined *)
  | Full (** show everything (title, summary, body if defined) *)
```

Do not duplicate comments between interface (mli files) and
implementation (ml) files. Expect the developer of the module to
consult both files. Limit mli comments to what is relevant to users
of the module.

# skeletor

Experimental project consisting of augmenting an organization's code bases
with a knowledge base made of semi-structured overlays that facilitate
navigation and understanding.

Progress is assessed by asking questions to an LLM-based agent with or
without the tool. Two main axes are considered:
- latency and token spend (cost)
- correctness (value)

A tentative score is of the form _value_/_cost_ over a representative set
of code bases and expert-level questions.

Examples of possible overlays:
- graph of interconnected claims with links to source code
- index of symbol definitions and uses allowing fast go-to-definition
  and go-to-uses navigation (if using an existing LSP isn't satisfying)

## Glossary

- **Anchor**: a persistent reference to a byte range within an indexed
  document, tracked automatically as the document is edited. Anchors let a
  claim point at a specific piece of content rather than a whole document;
  if the referenced text changes or moves, skeletor tries to relocate the
  anchor, and marks it stale if it can't.
- **Claim**: a node on the knowledge graph — a short title, a
  one-paragraph summary, and an optional longer Markdown body —
  describing a fact or piece of reasoning about the code base. When a body
  is given, the summary must be a compression of it (at most 1/4 of its
  length), not a separate text. Claims link to each other, to containers,
  and to anchors, forming an overlay on top of the source code.
- **Container**: a document identity (source + locator) used to represent
  either a real indexed document or a folder-like path prefix containing
  other documents; most containers are the latter, and are never
  themselves indexed. Linking a claim to a container means the claim
  depends on that document, or on everything under that folder.
- **Document**: a single piece of indexed text content (typically a source
  file), identified by its source and locator. skeletor keeps a copy of
  each document's current contents, plus a revision number that increments
  on every edit.
- **Locator**: a source-relative identifier for a document, e.g. a file
  path. Combined with a source, it uniquely identifies where a document
  lives.
- **Slice**: a selected region of a document or file — by byte range,
  row range,
  or row/column range — used for precise excerpting and rendering, e.g.
  when showing a piece of code as context for a claim or as a command's
  output.
- **Source**: where a corpus of documents comes from: a kind (`files`,
  `git`, or `github`) plus a name (syntax depending on the
  kind). Combined with a locator, a source identifies a specific document
  — analogous to a URL's scheme, domain, and path.

## Current status

This software has not been deployed in production. Breaking changes
will occur frequently.

## Installation

This is OCaml software with some external C libraries.
The project is compiled with Dune into an `skl` executable. Supported
platforms include Linux and MacOS. It is set up
for static linking against musl (libc alternative to glibc) on Alpine
Linux. This can be done directly via Docker with `make static`.
External dependencies are managed with Opam.

A development setup requires the following steps:

1. Install `opam`.
2. Install a suitable version of OCaml as specified in `dune-project`
   e.g. `opam switch create 5.5.1` for a global install. For a local
   install, use `opam switch create .`. This should select a suitable
   version of OCaml automatically.
3. Set your environment as instructed by `opam`:
   run `eval "$(opam env)"` in your shell to set `PATH` and other
   variables. Alternatively, running all the build commands
   with `opam exec -- <my command>` will work without messing with the
   environment.
4. Build and install the dependencies for your current Opam switch
   with `make setup`. At this stage, you will also have to install system
   dependencies (SQLite3, ...) if they're not already installed and
   detected on your system.
5. Build the project with `make` or `make build`. This makes the `skl`
   executable available as `./skl`.
6. Test the project with `make test`.
7. Optionally, run `make install` to install in `~/bin` or
   set `BINDIR` to install elsewhere e.g.
   `sudo BINDIR=/usr/local/bin make install`.

## Usage

The CLI is designed to be self-discoverable by an LLM-based agent or
by a human. So, try running `./skl` and do what it suggests.

The `howto` commands print instructions with concrete work budgets:

```sh
./skl howto update --effort standard --headlines 50 --headline-catchup 20
./skl howto update --effort 1.5
./skl howto update db.sqlite --effort auto
./skl howto build-recent --effort low
```

Effort accepts a non-negative numeric factor or an alias: `low=0.5`,
`standard=1.0`, `high=2.0`. Explicit budget options override the scaled
values, regardless of argument order. Tag budgets remain independent;
use `--new-tags` to change them. Run each command with `--help` to see
its budget options.

For `howto update`, `--effort auto` sums the files changed from each Git or
GitHub source's last indexed commit to its current HEAD and divides by 50.
This makes HEADLINES and CLAIMS equal to the changed-file count before explicit
overrides. It uses the supplied DB, or `db.sqlite` when omitted, without
refreshing indexes. Run it before `text documents update` advances the baselines.
Never-indexed SCM sources contribute all tracked files; Files sources contribute
zero. The estimate includes renames, formatting, deletions, and binary files.
Checkouts must be clean and on their registered branches; history or source
errors fail the estimate. Zero activity disables scaled work; use an explicit
`--headline-catchup` override or numeric effort to continue background maintenance.

`howto update` requires current headlines for new or meaningfully modified
source files and folders, with a `HEADLINES` cap of 50. Pure moves and verified
formatting-only changes are exempt from headline production. A separate
`HEADLINE_CATCHUP` target of 20 advances older coverage gaps even on an empty
diff. Use `--headlines` and `--headline-catchup` to override these budgets;
both follow effort scaling. CLAIMS also defaults to 50. Unfinished work is recorded for later updates.


Search indexed documents by topic with the bundled embedding model:

```sh
./skl text search-fuzzy DB "how do we handle retries" --max-results 5
```

Fuzzy embeddings are maintained with the other document indexes. Existing
corpora are backfilled automatically on first open. See
[base-libs/fuzzy](base-libs/fuzzy/README.md) for model provenance and limits.

Both document search commands accept `--source KIND:NAME` to search one
source. Add `--path PATH` to search a container and its descendants:

```sh
./skl text search-words DB "retry" --source files:myrepo --path lib
./skl text search-fuzzy DB "retry handling" --source files:myrepo --path lib
```

`--path` requires `--source`. Use `--path .` for the whole source, or an
exact document path for that document. Paths are relative to the source
and containers need not exist on disk.

Commands write basic execution logs under `logs/` in the workspace (after
`--chdir`). Filenames start with a local RFC-3339 timestamp captured at module
initialization with microsecond precision, followed by an optional numeric
disambiguator and the command name, for example
`2026-10-19T17:02:00.123456-07:00_skl_text_documents_update.log`.
Colons become underscores in filenames on Windows. Each entry starts with a
local timestamp at millisecond precision followed by a space
and the first message line. Continuation lines start with a space as well.
Files are created on the first log message; help and overview requests do not
create logs. Entries are flushed immediately. Logging assumes a single writer
per file; output failures warn once and let the command continue.

(* Relocate anchors and search snippets using unique shingles and local alignment.

   Normalize whitespace before extracting shingles. Ignore repeated shingles
   in both queries and documents. Index documents at stride 8 and query at
   stride 1.

   Require at least half the query's unique shingles, adjusted for the index
   stride, before considering a document. Select hits within 500 raw bytes
   of the most frequent query-minus-document offset. Choose the smallest
   offset on frequency ties. Align the original query bytes against the
   selected document window with Smith-Waterman. Whitespace gaps are free;
   other gaps cost one and substitutions cost two. Require the final
   range to span at least half the original query length after whitespace
   normalization of both strings.

   Failed attempts preserve anchor content and advance only the attempted
   revision. Successful attempts update both revision fields. Other edited
   documents may still have their previous indexed contents.
*)

open Printf
module T = App_types.Text

type doc_id = T.doc_id
type anchor_status = Up_to_date of Util.Text_source.t | Outdated

type anchor = {
  anchor_id : T.anchor_id;
  doc_id : T.doc_id;
  source_doc : T.source_doc;
  range : T.range;
  raw_contents : string;
  last_author : T.author;
  status : anchor_status;
  needs_review : bool;
}

module Set = Set.Make (struct
  type t = anchor

  let compare a b = compare a.anchor_id b.anchor_id
end)

(* Shingle length in normalized bytes.

   The 16-byte length and 8-byte stride balance index size and relocation
   accuracy on this repository. Whitespace normalization makes shingles
   denser and less sensitive to reindentation. See the borderline matching
   cases in [tests/Text_api_tests.ml] for accuracy checks. *)
let shingle_length = 16

(* Distance between indexed shingles, in normalized bytes. Adjacent
   shingles overlap by [shingle_length - shingle_offset] bytes.
   Queries use a stride of one byte. *)
let shingle_offset = 8

(* Allow up to 500 raw bytes of displacement on either side of the mode. *)
let match_offset_tolerance = 500

(* Minimum normalized anchor length needed to produce a query shingle.
   [add_anchor] also uses this as an early check on the raw byte length. *)
let min_anchor_length = shingle_length

(* Limit accidental whole-file anchors and their storage and matching cost.
   This fixed limit is separate from the configurable indexing file limit. *)
let max_anchor_length = 10 * 1024

(* A query needs at least one shingle after whitespace normalization. *)
let min_query_length = shingle_length

let get_doc_meta_exn db (src_doc : App_types.Src_doc.t) =
  let source_doc = App_types.Src_doc.to_source_doc src_doc in
  match
    DB.Documents.get_by_locator db ~source:source_doc.source
      source_doc.locator
  with
  | Some meta -> meta
  | None ->
      ksprintf failwith "Not indexed: %s" (App_types.Src_doc.show src_doc)

let to_public_anchor db (a : Internal_types.anchor) : anchor =
  let doc_meta, contents =
    match DB.Documents.get_full_by_id db a.doc_id with
    | Some x -> x
    | None -> failwith "Anchor references a nonexistent document"
  in
  (* Every edit must reconcile all anchors still on the document.
     Successful relocation advances both revision fields. Failure advances
     only [doc_revision_attempt]. A mismatch here violates that invariant. *)
  if a.doc_revision_attempt <> doc_meta.revision then
    ksprintf failwith
      "internal error: anchor %s's doc_revision_attempt (%d) does not match \
       document %s's revision (%d)"
      (App_types.Anchor_id.to_string a.anchor_id)
      a.doc_revision_attempt
      (App_types.Src_doc.show_source_doc doc_meta.source_doc)
      doc_meta.revision;
  let status =
    match contents with
    | DB.Deleted ->
        (* A deleted document cannot provide current context. *)
        Outdated
    | DB.Active contents ->
        if a.doc_revision = doc_meta.revision then
          Up_to_date
            { Util.Text_source.name = doc_meta.source_doc.locator; contents }
        else Outdated
  in
  let needs_review =
    match status with
    | Up_to_date _ -> false
    | Outdated -> (
        match a.acknowledged_revision with
        | None -> true
        | Some r -> r < doc_meta.revision)
        ~shingle:(Internal_types.Shingle_str.create shingle)
        ~range)

(* Each query shingle has one raw offset and at most one indexed occurrence
   per document. *)
type hit = {
  anchor_offset : int;
  query_start : int;
  doc_start : int;
  doc_end : int;
}

type candidate = {
  doc_id : T.doc_id;
  revision : int;
  contents : string;
  document_hits : int;
  num_hits : int;
  coverage : int;
  mode_offset : int;
  window : T.range;
  range : T.range;
}

let collect_hits db (anchor_norm : normalized) =
  let by_doc = Hashtbl.create 16 in
  let query_shingles = ref 0 in
  iter_shingles ~offset:1 anchor_norm.text (fun anchor_offset shingle ->
      incr query_shingles;
      DB.Shingles.find db (Internal_types.Shingle_str.create shingle)
      |> List.iter (fun (doc_id, (range : T.range)) ->
          let hit =
            {
              anchor_offset;
              query_start = anchor_norm.norm_to_raw.(anchor_offset);
              doc_start = range.start;
              doc_end = range.end_;
            }
          in
          let previous =
            Option.value (Hashtbl.find_opt by_doc doc_id) ~default:[]
          in
          Hashtbl.replace by_doc doc_id (hit :: previous)));
  (!query_shingles, by_doc)

(* Count matched query bytes once, even where overlapping shingles agree. *)
let hit_coverage hits =
  let sorted =
    List.sort (fun a b -> Int.compare a.anchor_offset b.anchor_offset) hits
  in
  let _, coverage =
    List.fold_left
      (fun (end_, total) hit ->
        let next_end = hit.anchor_offset + shingle_length in
        (next_end, total + next_end - max end_ hit.anchor_offset))
      (0, 0) sorted
  in
  coverage

(* Count equal raw displacements. Resolve frequency ties by signed offset,
   independently of hash-table iteration order. Hits are nonempty here. *)
let most_common_offset hits =
  let counts = Hashtbl.create 16 in
  List.iter
    (fun hit ->
      let offset = hit.query_start - hit.doc_start in
      let count = Option.value (Hashtbl.find_opt counts offset) ~default:0 in
      Hashtbl.replace counts offset (count + 1))
    hits;
  let offset, _ =
    Hashtbl.fold
      (fun offset count (best_offset, best_count) ->
        if count > best_count || (count = best_count && offset < best_offset)
        then (offset, count)
        else (best_offset, best_count))
      counts (max_int, 0)
  in
  offset

(* Bytewise alignment may stop inside a UTF-8 character. Realign within the
   narrowed target so the support count describes only the returned bytes. *)
let align_normalized query target =
  let rec align offset target =
    match Util.Smith_waterman.align Util.Smith_waterman.code query target with
    | None -> None
    | Some aligned ->
        let start, end_ =
          Util.Text.safe_range target ~start:aligned.target.start
            ~end_:aligned.target.end_
        in
        if start = aligned.target.start && end_ = aligned.target.end_ then
          Some
            {
              aligned with
              target = { start = offset + start; end_ = offset + end_ };
            }
        else if start >= end_ then None
        else align (offset + start) (String.sub target start (end_ - start))
  in
  align 0 target

let align_candidate ~query ~normalized_query (meta : T.doc_meta) contents hits
    =
  let mode_offset = most_common_offset hits in
  let selected =
    List.filter
      (fun hit ->
        abs (hit.query_start - hit.doc_start - mode_offset)
        <= match_offset_tolerance)
      hits
  in
  let start, end_ =
    List.fold_left
      (fun (start, end_) hit ->
        (min start hit.doc_start, max end_ hit.doc_end))
      (String.length contents, 0)
      selected
  in
  (* Include the query's predicted edges, not just the indexed hits. A name
     change near the beginning can otherwise hide the function header from
     alignment. Local alignment decides which boundary bytes still match. *)
  let start = min start (max 0 (-mode_offset)) in
  let end_ =
    max end_
      (min (String.length contents) (String.length query - mode_offset))
  in
  let window =
    {
      T.start = max 0 (start - shingle_length);
      end_ = min (String.length contents) (end_ + shingle_length);
    }
  in
  let start, end_ =
    Util.Text.safe_range contents ~start:window.start ~end_:window.end_
  in
  let window = { T.start; end_ } in
  (* A normalized shingle may span an arbitrarily long raw whitespace run.
     Enforce the displacement allowance on the whole window before alignment. *)
  let maximum_window =
    String.length query + (2 * match_offset_tolerance) + (2 * shingle_length)
  in
  if window.end_ - window.start > maximum_window then None
  else begin
    let target =
      normalize_whitespace
        (String.sub contents window.start (window.end_ - window.start))
    in
    match align_normalized normalized_query target.text with
    | None -> None
    | Some aligned ->
        let start, end_ =
          Util.Text.raw_range_of_normalized target ~start:aligned.target.start
            ~end_:aligned.target.end_
        in
        let start = window.start + start in
        let end_ = window.start + end_ in
        let minimum_length = (String.length normalized_query + 1) / 2 in
        if aligned.identical_bytes < minimum_length then None
        else
          Some
            {
              doc_id = meta.doc_id;
              revision = meta.revision;
              contents;
              document_hits = List.length hits;
              num_hits = List.length selected;
              coverage = hit_coverage selected;
              mode_offset;
              window;
              range = { T.start; end_ };
            }
  end

let compare_candidates a b =
  let c = Int.compare b.coverage a.coverage in
  if c <> 0 then c
  else
    let c = Int.compare b.num_hits a.num_hits in
    if c <> 0 then c else compare a.doc_id b.doc_id

let find_candidates db query anchor_norm =
  let query_shingles, by_doc = collect_hits db anchor_norm in
  (* Half the unique query shingles, adjusted for the document stride. *)
  let minimum_hits =
    max 1 ((query_shingles + (2 * shingle_offset) - 1) / (2 * shingle_offset))
  in
  let rejected = ref 0 in
  let candidates =
    Hashtbl.fold
      (fun doc_id hits acc ->
        if List.length hits < minimum_hits then (
          incr rejected;
          acc)
        else
          match DB.Documents.get_full_by_id db doc_id with
          | None ->
              failwith
                (sprintf "anchor relocation error: missing document in db: %s"
                   (App_types.Doc_id.to_string doc_id))
          | Some (_, DB.Deleted) -> acc
          | Some (meta, DB.Active contents) -> (
              match
                align_candidate ~query ~normalized_query:anchor_norm.text meta
                  contents hits
              with
              | None ->
                  incr rejected;
                  acc
              | Some candidate -> candidate :: acc))
      by_doc []
  in
  ( query_shingles,
    minimum_hits,
    !rejected,
    List.sort compare_candidates candidates )

let preview text =
  let len = String.length text in
  if len <= 2048 then text
  else
    String.sub text 0 1024 ^ "\n...[truncated]...\n"

(* Failed attempts preserve the old range and contents. The caller owns the
   transaction containing both the document update and anchor relocation. *)
let relocate_one db (a : Internal_types.anchor) ~doc_revision =
  let anchor_norm = normalize_whitespace a.raw_contents in
  let query_shingles, minimum_hits, rejected, candidates =
    find_candidates db a.raw_contents anchor_norm
  in
  log_relocation_candidates db a ~doc_revision ~anchor_norm ~query_shingles
    ~minimum_hits ~rejected candidates;
  match candidates with
  | [] ->
      DB.Anchors.mark_attempt_failed db a.anchor_id
        ~doc_revision_attempt:doc_revision;
      None
  | candidate :: _ ->
      let range = candidate.range in
      let raw_contents =
        String.sub candidate.contents range.start (range.end_ - range.start)
      in
      let changed =
        candidate.doc_id <> a.doc_id
        || range <> a.range
        || raw_contents <> a.raw_contents
      in
      let updated =
        {
          a with
          doc_id = candidate.doc_id;
          doc_revision = candidate.revision;
          doc_revision_attempt = candidate.revision;
          range;
          raw_contents;
          last_author = T.Algo;
        }
      in
      Util.Log.printf
        "Anchor relocation %s applying relocation: document=%s revision=%d \
         range=B%d-%d changed=%b; previous anchor content still intact"
        (App_types.Anchor_id.to_string a.anchor_id)
        (App_types.Doc_id.to_string candidate.doc_id)
        candidate.revision range.start range.end_ changed;
      DB.Anchors.relocate db updated;
      if changed then Some updated else None

let relocate_stale_anchors db ~doc_id ~doc_revision : anchor list =
  DB.Anchors.get_stale db doc_id ~doc_revision
  |> List.filter_map (fun a -> relocate_one db a ~doc_revision)
  |> List.map (to_public_anchor db)

item.text:
If the anchor text matches in multiple files, relocation ranks the candidates by shingle coverage, then hit count. If those scores tie, it chooses the candidate with the lowest document ID. It then moves the anchor there without flagging the ambiguity. [Candidate ranking](/workspace/kb-research/samples/skeletor/skeletor-sitemap/src/skeletor/base-libs/text/Anchor.ml:348) and [relocation](/workspace/kb-research/samples/skeletor/skeletor-sitemap/src/skeletor/base-libs/text/Anchor.ml:483) show this behavior.

That is undesirable when copies of the text are unrelated: an exact match alone cannot establish which file the anchor refers to. The tests document a known false positive where an anchor moves to an unrelated file containing the same block. [Regression test](/workspace/kb-research/samples/skeletor/skeletor-sitemap/src/skeletor/base-libs/text/tests/Text_api_tests.ml:1096). Ambiguous matches should be surfaced for review rather than silently resolved by document ID.
